page: Microsoft Azure FX8-4mds_v2 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores with hyper-threading. The processor operates at a base frequency of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. The server is equipped with 168.0 GB of RAM, yielding 42.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled with a 472 GB local disk, and the instance supports Premium Storage. No GPUs are included.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server achieves top-tier single-core results, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2355.0 and strong single-threaded gzip compression of 34.91 GB/sec. However, multi-core performance is limited by the 4-vCPU allocation, resulting in a weak stress-ng multi-core score of 4441.77 and weak software compilation performance. Memory bandwidth is average for small cached blocks at 344.91 GB/sec but drops to weak for large uncached blocks.

The qualitative cost profile of the FX8-4mds_v2 is defined by its high memory density relative to its compute footprint. This resource allocation makes it highly efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing, such as medium-sized in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, and single-threaded text processing. It is less suitable for highly parallelized tasks, software compilation, or large-scale LLM inference.
